prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals and targets

Public finances and taxation
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18; debt to fall as a share of GDP thereafter.
- New fiscal rules: allow borrowing for productive investment while keeping day-to-day spending balanced over the cycle.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; consider aligning the employee National Insurance threshold.
- Anti-avoidance measures, a time‑limited banking surcharge, reforms to reliefs, and a levy on residential properties over £2m.

Economy, industry and infrastructure
- Double economy‑wide innovation and research spending; protect the science budget in real terms.
- Expand the British Business Bank; promote competition, community and alternative finance.
- Devolve more economic powers locally; use procurement to support SMEs.
- Ten‑year rolling infrastructure plans; HS2 and major rail upgrades; wider rail electrification; improved regional links; expand light rail.
- Complete high‑speed broadband rollout to 99.9% of premises; support scale‑ups and digital skills.

Energy and climate
- Legally binding net‑zero greenhouse gas target by 2050; power‑sector decarbonisation range of 50–100g CO2/kWh by 2030.
- Stimulate at least £100bn private low‑carbon investment by 2020; expand the Green Investment Bank with borrowing powers.
- End unabated coal by 2025; progress carbon capture and storage; support renewables, storage, smart grids and community energy; accept new nuclear without public subsidy.
- Strict shale regulation; allocate 50% of shale tax revenues to a Low‑carbon Transition Fund.

Work, welfare and pensions
- Complete Universal Credit; devolve and improve back‑to‑work support; review sanctions with a “yellow card” warning.
- Temporary 1% cap on working‑age benefit uprating until 2017/18 (disability and parental benefits exempt).
- Improve flexible working, pay transparency, minimum wage enforcement; promote a Living Wage in central government.
- Protect and legislate the State Pension “triple lock”; complete auto‑enrolment; review a single rate of pensions tax relief.

Families, childcare and education
- 20 hours’ free childcare for ages two to four, and for working parents from end of paid leave; tax‑free childcare and 85% UC childcare support.
- Protect education funding from early years to 19; fair national funding formula; extend Pupil Premium; qualified teachers in every class.
- New core curriculum including PSHE/financial literacy; independent standards authority; teacher development entitlement.
- Double the number of businesses hiring apprentices; expand higher apprenticeships; discount bus pass for 16–21s.
- Widen university participation; protect and extend postgraduate income‑contingent loans; review student finance.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS England funding by at least £8bn real by 2020; expand GP access and community pharmacy roles.
- Equal priority for mental health: waiting‑time standards, crisis care, perinatal and children’s services; +£500m a year by 2016/17.
- Pool NHS and social care budgets locally by 2018; integrate services; reform payment to reward prevention.
- Support carers: £250 annual bonus; explore paid care leave; raise Carer’s Allowance earnings limit.

Housing
- Target 300,000 homes/year; new garden cities/towns; use public land; a Housing Investment Bank; direct commissioning where needed.
- Strengthen plan‑led development; focus on brownfield; self‑build registers; curb “buy to leave”.
- More council/affordable homes; flexible borrowing; intermediate options (Affordable Rent, Shared Ownership, Rent to Own).
- Private renting: longer tenancies with inflation‑linked increases; licensing; curb excessive letting fees; deposit loans for under‑30 first‑time renters.
- Home energy efficiency: aim for EPC Band C for all homes by 2035 (low‑income by 2027); council tax incentives; revamped Green Homes Loan.

Rights, policing, justice and drugs
- Digital Bill of Rights; protect Human Rights Act; stronger oversight of surveillance and undercover policing; press freedom safeguards.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; tougher response to violence against women and girls.
- Presumption against short short-term prison sentences; expand community sentences; specialist drug courts.
- Treat drug possession for personal use primarily as a health issue; allow medicinal cannabis prescribing.

Devolution, democracy and external affairs
- Constitutional Convention; proportional representation (STV) for local and Westminster elections; votes at 16; party donation cap of £10,000.
- Implement further devolution to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; “Devolution on Demand” in England.
- Remain engaged in EU reform; complete Single Market in key sectors; support fair trade deals with protections.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; strengthen tax transparency; pursue binding climate agreements; adjust nuclear posture away from continuous patrols.
